1A.clue: Yellow booth where you watched the meter tick on an STD call
1A.easy: Public Call Office, in three letters
1A.why: PCO meant Public Call Office. STD calls were cheaper late at night, so the queue started after 11.

4A.clue: The dhol gives it, and your heart skips one when your crush says hi
4A.easy: Rhythm of a song, or of your heart
4A.why: 'Skip a beat': your heart does it, the baraat dhol never does.

5A.clue: Bread that got a tan, or a glass raised at the sangeet
5A.why: Breakfast and a speech, one word.

6A.why: Har ek = each. Small word, big glue in a grid.

7A.clue: What she did, and left no crumbs
7A.why: Gen Z slang: if she 'ate and left no crumbs', she nailed it.

1D.clue: Shanti, or the two-finger selfie pose
1D.why: The V-sign went from 1960s protest posters to every group selfie.

2D.clue: What the sabziwala wants when UPI says "server down"
2D.why: UPI rules the market, until the server goes down.

3D.clue: Where Friday releases now land without a ticket queue
3D.why: OTT stands for Over The Top: streamed straight to you, skipping cable.

4D.clue: Floats on Dal Lake, or plugs into a Gen Z's ears
4D.why: boAt, the Indian earphone brand, and the shikaras of Dal Lake share a name.

5D.clue: Chai in English, or gossip in Gen Z
5D.why: 'Spill the tea' means share the gossip.

1A.easy: Surname shared by Kiran and P V Narasimha
1A.why: Kiran Rao's Laapataa Ladies was India's official Oscar entry for the 2025 Academy Awards.

4A.clue: You hear it in a theatre, and it's how you sleep after Sunday biryani
4A.easy: Noise, or healthy, as in a ___ mind
4A.why: Two meanings in one word: noise, and solid, as in a sound sleep.

6A.clue: Ameen Sayani's Binaca Geetmala came out of this box
6A.easy: Vividh Bharati and FM play on it
6A.why: Binaca Geetmala, hosted by Ameen Sayani, was the country's favourite countdown show for decades.

7A.clue: Rancho's gang had three of these
7A.why: 3 Idiots (2009): Rancho, Farhan and Raju. Aal izz well.

8A.clue: Beta in English, and the one asked "shaadi kab karoge?"
8A.why: Every Indian son's annual exam: the shaadi question at family functions.

1D.clue: Where potholes live, and they multiply every monsoon
1D.why: Monsoon plus roads equals potholes, a national tradition.

2D.clue: ___ note, sent when you're too lazy to type
2D.why: Voice notes: loved by senders, feared by listeners.

3D.clue: Makes you cry in the kitchen, and has made governments cry at the ballot box
3D.why: Soaring onion prices are widely blamed for the BJP's 1998 Delhi election loss.

4D.why: The Palk Strait separates Tamil Nadu from Sri Lanka.

5D.clue: Shape of a bindi, and the end of every sentence
5D.easy: A tiny round mark, like a full stop
5D.why: A bindi and a full stop share one shape.

1A.clue: Arrives in a red cylinder, carried up by a man who never takes the lift
1A.why: The LPG cylinder was India's most awaited home delivery long before Swiggy.

4A.clue: Mummy drops one for weeks before her birthday, and nobody picks it up
4A.why: Indian mothers drop hints for weeks. The family still asks 'kya chahiye?' the night before.

5A.clue: What your train ticket must be, and Gen Z's way of saying 'fair point'
5A.easy: Legally acceptable, like a ticket or an argument
5A.why: 'That's valid' is Gen Z for 'fair enough'.

6A.clue: ___ station: where the British ran from the plains every summer
6A.why: Shimla was the summer capital of British India.

7A.why: Sridevi starred in Yash Chopra's Chandni (1989).

1D.clue: Danda's partner in the original gully sport
1D.why: Gilli-danda: one stick, one peg and at least one broken window.

2D.clue: Kapoor who has been saying 'jhakaas' for decades
2D.why: 'Jhakaas' has been Anil Kapoor's catchphrase for decades.

3D.clue: Three letters on the yellow board, next to ISD and PCO
3D.why: STD stood for Subscriber Trunk Dialling.

4D.clue: What the barber cuts while explaining national politics
4D.why: Every Indian barber is also a political analyst.

5D.clue: Tape you rented on Sunday and rewound before returning
5D.why: Video parlours rented out VHS tapes, and you were expected to rewind them first.
